instructions: This is a Twilio-based call center for a rental homes business. Review with these hard-won domain invariants in mind, each learned from a production incident: (1) Every <Gather> must have a fallback in the SAME TwiML document (voicemail <Record> or explicit next step) — a Gather timeout with nothing after it silently drops the caller. (2) Never eject or redirect a caller who may already be bridged to an agent; always verify queue membership (stillQueued) before a REST redirect, or a live conversation gets hung up. (3) The queue wait cap must be enforced by a server-side timer, not only the waitUrl — Twilio re-requests the waitUrl only after the hold-music file finishes (~80s), so waitUrl-only checks let callers hold far past the cap. (4) Presence semantics: logged in + heartbeating IS online; only signing out makes an agent offline. A stale-marked agent must be revived by any heartbeat, restoring oncall (not available) if they were mid-call. (5) Voice SDK access tokens must have a TTL matching the 12h session — a shorter token silently expires mid-shift and the agent's phone stops ringing. (6) Agent identity must always come from the server-verified session (req.user), never from client-supplied strings — it lands in CRM records. (7) Zoho rejects unknown picklist values and drops the ENTIRE record — never write new picklist values without confirming they exist in Zoho first. (8) Caller ID on a Retell transfer leg is Retell's number, not the caller's — never treat From as the caller's real number on transferred calls. (9) Every bridged <Dial> needs a timeLimit — the 4h default runs up call, recording, and transcription costs on stuck bridges. (10) Static assets are cached; bumping the ?v= query version in index.html is required for JS/CSS changes to reach agents.
